subject: Audit Snapshot Packaging & Chain-of-Custody RFI
messages:
From: Ian Murphy <ian.murphy@brightbank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Audit snapshot packaging, transport and chain-of-custody

Hi Ben,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look at our audit-export requirements. As part of BrightBank's vendor risk evaluation we need a short, technical response covering:

- Supported export serialization formats (NDJSON, Parquet, Avro, tar/gzip, etc.) and whether full record-level metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model version, route ID) is preserved.
- Integrity/tamper evidence: do you provide signed manifests, per-file hashes (SHA256), and an auditable sequence or monotonic offset so we can detect missing records?
- Transport options: S3 direct-to-bucket with presigned PUTs, SFTP, physical media shipping, or a managed transfer service? Any throughput SLAs for large exports (10–50 TB)?
- Retention controls: per-account retention windows and legal-hold overrides; how are deletions performed and justified in audit logs?
- Chain-of-custody: can you provide a Certificate of Export (signed by Redwood) that includes hashes, timestamps, and operator identifiers?
- Delivery timing: typical lead time to schedule and deliver a bulk export for an active production tenant.

We'd like a response by EOD Wednesday so we can include it in our vendor scorecard. I'm cc'ing procurement (procurement@brightbank.com) who will follow on commercial questions.

Attachment: BrightBank-RFP-Annex-A.pdf (BrightBank questionnaire)

Thanks,
Ian Murphy
Senior Information Security Manager
BrightBank, Inc.

Subject: Re: RFI: Audit snapshot packaging, transport and chain-of-custody

Ian — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide detail and a pragmatic path to a canary export so you can validate the artifacts. High-level answers inline; Kimberly (security) will follow up with the technical manifest and integrity details. Vivek and I can coordinate scheduling and commercial items with Marissa.

Quick bullets to address your asks:
- Formats: we support NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) and gzipped tar bundles containing NDJSON or Parquet payloads. Exports include full per-record metadata (ISO8601 timestamps, request_id, model_id, model_version, route_id).
- Integrity: exports are delivered with a signed manifest that lists files, SHA256 checksums, and a monotonic sequence number. Manifests are PGP-signed and we can provide a notarized hash on request.
- Transport: primary option is direct S3 delivery via pre-provisioned customer bucket + role/ACL. We also support SFTP and AWS Snowball for very large volumes. Typical throughput for S3 bulk exports can reach multiple TB/hr depending on size and parallelism; Kimberly will give an estimated SLA approach.
- Retention: retention is configurable per-account. Defaults for hosted customers are 90 days for operational audit logs; Reserved/Dedicated customers can configure longer windows and archival tiers. We support legal-hold flags that prevent deletion until cleared and emit preservation events to the audit ledger.
- Chain-of-custody: we provide a Certificate of Export (PDF) that references manifest hashes, timestamps, and operator IDs. We can also provide signed S3 event receipts if you prefer MD5/SHA256 proof of delivery.
- Timing: typical lead time for a scheduled bulk export is 5–10 business days for up to 5 TB; larger jobs require 10–20 business days depending on throughput and any required validations.

I've attached a short spec (Redwood-Audit-Spec-v1.0.pdf) and asked Kimberly to add the manifest sample and recommended handoff steps. If that timeline looks tight for your procurement calendar, Marissa will follow to propose terms and a cost outline.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: Audit snapshot packaging, transport and chain-of-custody — technical details

Ian / team — adding the technical details you're looking for. Below are specifics we include in our standard export flow and options for higher-assurance customers.

1) Supported payload formats
- NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) — default for row-level audit export; each record contains: timestamp_utc (ISO8601), event_type, request_id, customer_id, model_id, model_version, route_id, token_count, user-provided metadata.
- Parquet — columnar format for analytic portability (schema exported alongside files).
- Container delivery: .tar.gz bundles (name includes time range and monotonic sequence).

2) File-level integrity and tamper evidence
- SHA256 checksums for each file are computed at generation time and included in the manifest.
- Manifest format: compact JSON lines document listing file entries: {"file":"path/to/file","sha256":"...","records":123456,"first_ts":"2026-05-01T00:00:00Z","last_ts":"2026-05-16T00:00:00Z","sequence_start":10001,"sequence_end":22345}.
- Manifests are signed with an organizational PGP key (and can be optionally countersigned by our HSM-backed KMS).
- We maintain an export ledger (immutable append-only) that records export job metadata, operator id, and a root hash of the manifest. That ledger entry can be provided as part of the Certificate of Export.

3) Transport & delivery options
- S3 direct-to-bucket (recommended): we provision a lifecycle role and deliver into your bucket. We support multipart parallel uploads to scale throughput.
- SFTP: server-to-server transfer with client cert auth.
- Snowball / physical transfer: for >20 TB where network egress is impractical.
- Managed transfer: we can coordinate with your MFT vendor and emit additional delivery receipts.

4) Retention controls and deletion semantics
- Per-account configurable retention with tiered archival: hot (0–90d), cold (90–730d), archive (>730d).
- Deletion is a two-step operation: scheduled deletion job + audit entry. Legal-hold sets a preservation flag preventing scheduling. All deletion operations are recorded in the audit ledger with operator and justification.

5) Chain-of-custody artifacts
- Certificate of Export (PDF): includes manifest root hash, time (UTC), operator id, export job id, PGP signature reference, and notarization fields if requested.
- Delivery receipts: S3 event records or signed transfer logs for SFTP/Snowball.
- Optional: notarization via third-party timestamping service (RFC 3161) on manifest root hash.

6) Throughput / SLA guidance (typical)
- Small export (<=5 TB): 5–10 business days; we perform schema validation and a single canary bundle.
- Medium export (5–20 TB): 10–15 business days; staged parallel export jobs and verification.
- Large export (>20 TB): 15–30 business days; recommend Snowball or coordinated MFT windows. We can provide an engineering runbook and an on-call escort for high-risk jobs.

7) Proof-of-delivery & verification
- We publish per-file SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest. Customers can verify checksums after download and request our manifest signature for validation.

Attachment: export-manifest-sample.json (example manifest snippet)

If you'd like, we can run a 1–2 hour technical validation session with your infra team and then schedule a canary export. Proposal: schedule call this week and target a canary export next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — that level of detail is exactly what we needed. A couple of clarifications before we route this to internal legal/procurement: 

1) Can you confirm whether the export ledger is independently auditable (i.e., do you provide a read-only copy or hashed proof we can retain for our records)?
2) For large exports using S3, can you provide a 3rd-party transfer estimate (TB/hr) for a typical 8-thread multipart upload from us-east-1 to us-east-1? We want to model egress windows.
3) Procurement asks whether you can include a Certificate of Export as part of the standard SOW for enterprise customers (signed and attached at job completion).

Ian / procurement — short answers and next steps: 

1) Export ledger auditability: we provide a downloadable proof bundle containing the manifest(s), signed root hash, and a read-only ledger extract (signed) that you can ingest into your archive. For very high assurance customers we can provide a time-stamped notarization of the root hash.

2) Transfer throughput estimate (8-thread multipart upload, us-east-1 -> us-east-1): 0.8–1.2 TB/hour per concurrent worker depending on object size and network characteristics. With a 16-worker parallelization we routinely see 12–18 TB/hour in our staging tests; expect diminishing returns beyond network/IO limits. We'll provide a transfer estimate tailored to your tenant during the scheduling call.

3) Certificate of Export in SOW: yes — we can add a clause that Redwood will deliver a signed Certificate of Export upon completion of each bulk export job as part of our enterprise SOW. Marissa will follow up on commercial language and timeline.

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 60-min technical validation with BrightBank infra (Kimberly + Vivek) — please share 2 time slots.
- Run a 1 GB canary export to your test bucket (no PII) within 3 business days of the call.
- After successful canary, schedule full export window and agree on delivery SLA in the SOW.

Attachment: canary-export-plan.xlsx (high-level runbook and checklist)
